what_was_built.api: kb.catalog.parsers.docx_parser.parse_docx(path, *, source_id) and parse_docx_bytes(data, *, source_id) return a DocxParseResult: fragments, unsupported, covered, counts, archive and the parser/library identity. resolve_locator(document, locator) navigates a locator again from scratch and returns the text plus the live XML element, or None.
what_was_built.locator_meaning: paragraph=N is exactly Document.paragraphs[N-1] (every w:p child of w:body, including the empty ones, because an address that skips a blank paragraph is off by one for everything after it). table=N is exactly Document.tables[N-1]. cell=(R,C) is the cell whose w:tc ORIGIN is at grid row R, column C, 1-based. chapter is the text of the nearest preceding outline heading, taken from w:outlineLvl first and from the heading style id second.
what_was_built.no_pages: file_page, printed_label, spine, snapshot_url and snapshot_at are None on every DOCX locator. kb.contracts refuses a printed label standing in for a page; the kb.fragment CHECK constraint refuses a docx_* row that carries a file_page at all, and both refusals are exercised against the running server.
what_was_built.merged_cells: One fragment per origin w:tc, addressed at its top-left grid position. Every covered grid position is reported in DocxParseResult.covered with the address that owns it and gets no fragment. This is the difference the card is about: enumerating the grid by column returns the SAME _Cell object at every column a merge spans, so the naive reading of merged_cells.docx yields nine cell fragments for seven cells, two of them duplicates carrying identical text.
what_was_built.nested_tables: Reported in DocxParseResult.unsupported with the inner table's own text intact, and given no fragment. Locator carries one table number and no nesting depth, so any locator for the inner table would be an address nothing else in the system could resolve. The owning cell's fragment holds only that cell's own paragraphs, and the outer table's rendering marks the cell [nested table] so the content is not silently absent.
what_was_built.other_constructs: Text boxes, tracked deletions, inline and body-level content controls, w:altChunk and paragraphs nested past 64 levels are each reported rather than guessed at, and none is dropped silently. Tracked insertions and field RESULTS are read (they are text the document shows); w:delText and w:instrText are not (deleted text is not in the document, a field code is an instruction). mc:AlternateContent is read once, from mc:Choice, so a drawing is not printed twice.
what_was_built.archive_limits: Checked from the ZIP central directory before any part is inflated: file size, part count, total uncompressed size, overall expansion ratio, per-part expansion ratio for parts over 1 MiB, member names that are not plain relative paths, encrypted members, and the presence of [Content_Types].xml and word/document.xml. Every limit is a refusal, never a truncation: a refused container produces no fragments at all.
what_was_built.fragment_identity: uuid5 over (source_id, ordinal), not uuid4. Parsing the same bytes twice for the same source produces the same ids, so a re-parse is recognisable as a re-parse against the UNIQUE (source_id, ordinal) constraint instead of quietly becoming a second set of rows.
what_was_built.rendering: A table fragment keeps the grid shape: one line per grid row, one field per grid column, '[merged]' for a covered position, '[nested table]' for a cell that also holds one. A cell with several paragraphs keeps them newline-separated in its own fragment and joins them with ' / ' in the table rendering.

central_invariant.mutation_tested: Thirteen defects were injected one at a time into the three card modules and the whole tests/integration/parsers suite was run after each; all thirteen were rejected by a named test, and the tree was verified green again afterwards. (1) numbering only paragraphs that have text -> test_paragraph_n_is_exactly_document_paragraphs_n_minus_one. (2) emitting a fragment for every covered grid position -> test_a_merged_cell_is_emitted_once_at_its_origin_and_never_at_a_covered_position. (3) giving the nested table a fragment of its own -> test_no_fragment_anywhere_claims_the_nested_table_as_a_top_level_one. (4) stamping file_page=1 on every DOCX locator -> test_no_docx_locator_carries_a_page_a_label_or_a_snapshot. (5) resolving an out-of-range paragraph to the nearest one instead of None -> test_a_locator_that_names_nothing_resolves_to_none_and_not_to_a_neighbour. (6) stopping the heading-scope tracking -> test_a_fragment_is_filed_under_the_heading_it_sits_under. (7) recognising only the space-separated spelling of a heading style -> test_a_fragment_is_filed_under_the_heading_it_sits_under. (8) disabling the per-part expansion ratio check -> test_a_single_part_that_expands_a_thousandfold_is_refused_even_when_the_archive_does_not. (9) treating a w:vMerge continuation as a fresh cell -> test_every_covered_position_is_reported_with_the_address_that_owns_it. (10) removing the XML depth guard -> test_a_paragraph_nested_past_the_depth_limit_is_reported_not_half_read. (11) reading w:delText as content -> test_tracked_deletion_is_excluded_from_the_text_and_reported. (12) reading both branches of mc:AlternateContent -> test_a_field_result_is_read_once_and_its_instruction_never_is. (13) addressing a merged cell at its LAST covered column instead of its origin -> test_a_merged_cell_is_emitted_once_at_its_origin_and_never_at_a_covered_position. Two earlier mutation rounds were discarded rather than reported: one was written with escaped newlines that never matched the source, and one ran against a tree that had a real failing test of its own, so every 'caught' in it was contamination. checks.reason: 9 tests. Fragments are INSERTed through every column kb.fragment has, read back, turned into a Locator again and resolved against the document. The RLS read leg runs over a pool connected as kb_app with app.principal set and a real library_grant, and a principal with no grant sees zero rows. The file_page refusal is the server's own CheckViolation text, not a restatement of it.

checks.name: runtime_write_path_for_fragments
checks.reason: There is no runtime write path to exercise, and that is a finding rather than a missing test. kb.fragment has RLS enabled and forced with exactly one policy, fragment_read, which is SELECT only; there is no INSERT policy, and kb_worker is granted only SELECT, UPDATE on kb.job and SELECT on kb.source. Observed against a real PostgreSQL 16.2 with the full migration set: `SET ROLE kb_app; set_config('app.principal', ...); INSERT INTO kb.fragment ...` returns SQLSTATE 42501 'new row violates row-level security policy for table "fragment"', and the same INSERT as kb_worker returns SQLSTATE 42501 'permission denied for table fragment'. So a parsed fragment cannot be written by any runtime role as the schema stands. This card writes its rows through the migration role in its tests and does not assert the refusal, because a test asserting that a defect exists would start failing the day someone fixes it. The one-line fix is in contract_change_proposals.

contract_change_proposals.finding: kb.fragment has columns id, source_id, ordinal, locator_kind, file_page, printed_label, chapter, paragraph, snapshot_url, snapshot_at, text. There is no column for a table number and no column for a cell, so the two of the three DOCX locator kinds this card is required to produce — DOCX_TABLE and DOCX_CELL — cannot be persisted as addresses. kb.contracts.entities.Locator has had `table: int | None` and `cell: tuple[int, int] | None` since the contracts were written; the DDL never caught up. Read from information_schema.columns on a real server: the eleven columns above, and no 'table' and no 'cell'.
contract_change_proposals.proposed_change: In the next migration, add to kb.fragment: `table_no integer CHECK (table_no IS NULL OR table_no >= 1)`, `cell_row integer CHECK (cell_row IS NULL OR cell_row >= 1)`, `cell_col integer CHECK (cell_col IS NULL OR cell_col >= 1)`, and `CONSTRAINT cell_coordinates_are_all_or_none CHECK ((cell_row IS NULL) = (cell_col IS NULL))`. No CHECK should tie a cell to a table without also allowing the table to be absent, because a nested table has no table number and must be storable as an explicit absence rather than as a half-address.
contract_change_proposals.action_taken: Not applied: migrations/ is outside this card's allowed paths and has a single owner. The parser emits the full Locator including table and cell, and the storage gap is proved rather than worked around. test_the_fragment_table_has_no_column_for_a_table_or_a_cell_address states the current column set and is documented as a marker that is expected to fail the day the columns exist.

contract_change_proposals.finding: kb.fragment is RLS-enabled and FORCEd with exactly one policy, fragment_read, which is FOR SELECT. There is no INSERT policy, so a fragment cannot be written by any runtime role: kb_app gets SQLSTATE 42501 'new row violates row-level security policy for table "fragment"', and kb_worker gets 42501 'permission denied for table fragment' because 0002 grants it no INSERT on this table at all. The extraction pipeline this card feeds therefore has nowhere to put its output. This is the same class of gap C10 found and narrowly worked around for kb.source_version, which suggests it is worth one sweep of every content table rather than one card at a time.
contract_change_proposals.proposed_change: Add `CREATE POLICY fragment_write ON kb.fragment FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM kb.source s WHERE s.id = source_id AND kb.role_rank(kb.effective_role(kb.current_principal(), s.library_id)) >= 20));` — contributor or better, mirroring source_write — and grant INSERT on kb.fragment to kb_worker in the role-grant migration, since kb_worker is the role a parse job would run as. Whether a *worker* should need a principal at all is a separate policy question for the same owner.
contract_change_proposals.action_taken: Not applied: migrations/ is outside this card's allowed paths and has a single owner. C12A's tests write fragments through the migration role and say so in the module docstring; the read path is still exercised for real, as kb_app, through fragment_read.

contract_change_proposals.finding: The size and archive limits are this card's proposal, not a number quoted from anywhere: PRODUCT-SPEC states no figure. The defaults are 64 MiB container, 256 MiB expanded, 200:1 overall expansion, 200:1 per part over 1 MiB, 4096 parts. A brand guideline book with a lot of embedded imagery can sit near 64 MiB, and the per-part ratio in particular is a heuristic — a legitimate XML part that happens to compress very well would be refused. They are parameters, not constants: ArchiveLimits is a frozen dataclass that a caller passes in, so the owner can raise them per deployment without touching this code.
contract_change_proposals.proposed_change: The single owner of deployment configuration should confirm the four numbers against the real corpus, and decide whether they belong in PRODUCT-SPEC or in a per-library quota. Until then they are documented defaults with a named owner.
contract_change_proposals.action_taken: Implemented, configurable, tested, and called out here rather than presented as a specification.

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: A nested table is reported rather than located, and the report carries its text. That is a deliberate loss of addressability: the inner table's content is recoverable by a human reading DocxParseResult.unsupported, but a retrieval system cannot point a citation at it. If that matters, the honest fix is a contract change — a nesting depth on Locator, or a separate docx_nested_cell kind — not a second numbering scheme invented inside a parser.
findings_for_the_next_owner.action_taken: The conservative choice, stated in the module docstring and in the dataclass. test_nothing_is_lost_between_the_fragments_and_the_report proves the text is there.

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: The text walk is a deliberate superset of python-docx's Paragraph.text. It reads w:ins and w:fldSimple, which python-docx skips, and it reads w:hyperlink, which python-docx 1.2.0 does handle. The consequence is that a paragraph containing a tracked insertion or a field result extracts more here than it would through the library's own .text. That is the intended reading — a tracked insertion is text the document shows — but it means the parser and the library disagree on some documents, and anyone comparing the two will find a difference that is not a bug.
findings_for_the_next_owner.action_taken: Documented at the function and in the module docstring; the exotic_runs.docx fixture makes the difference visible and test_a_field_result_is_read_once_and_its_instruction_never_is pins the field half.

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: Heading detection reads w:outlineLvl first because it is the language-neutral definition of the outline, and falls back to the style id matching ^heading[\s_-]*([1-9])$. A document whose headings use a localised style id and carry no explicit outline level yields chapter=None for every fragment. That is honest — chapter is a real field and None is a real answer — but a German Word file with default styles may well land there.
findings_for_the_next_owner.action_taken: Not solved; it needs a style-name translation table, which is a different concern from addressing and would be better owned with the rest of the DOCX support. The None case is tested so that it stays a reported answer rather than a silent misfiling.

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: A DOCX is not byte-reproducible by default: ZIP stores a per-entry modification time taken from the clock, so two rebuilds seconds apart differ. An earlier determinism check here passed by accident, because both runs landed inside the same second, and the honest check is what caught it — test_the_builder_and_the_committed_fixtures_agree compares SHA-256 against a fresh rebuild and failed until the builder was fixed.
findings_for_the_next_owner.action_taken: The builder now rewrites each package with a fixed 1980-01-01 timestamp after saving. The same trap applies to C11's EPUB fixtures and to C12B's HTML fixtures and is worth knowing before someone else spends an hour on it.

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: The suite is loaded with `pytest_plugins = ["docx_fixtures"]` in each module rather than a conftest.py, because the card's allowed path is tests/integration/parsers/docx* and a file called conftest.py does not match it. pytest prints one PytestAssertRewriteWarning for docx_fixtures as a result. It is cosmetic. If the integrator later prefers a conftest.py, moving docx_fixtures.py content into tests/integration/parsers/conftest.py and deleting the pytest_plugins lines is the whole change.
findings_for_the_next_owner.action_taken: Left as is, with the reasoning recorded here rather than worked around with a sys.path hack.

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: A w:vMerge continuation with no w:val="restart" above it is inconsistent XML. The parser treats it as the start of its own cell and raises an orphan_vmerge note rather than guessing which row it belongs to, and a w:tblGrid that disagrees with the rows actually used raises grid_width_mismatch. Neither shape appears in the synthetic fixtures, so both notes are exercised only through code review here, not by a test.
findings_for_the_next_owner.action_taken: Documented and left untested rather than tested against a hand-built malformed file. If a real corpus produces these, they become fixtures.
